title: Cooking Okra Soup With My Grandma

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Hi Grandpa! How have you been lately?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Good morning, my dear Nubuke! I'm doing well, thank you for asking. I woke up bright and early today, ready to spend some lovely time with you. As for cooking, I was thinking we could make your favorite dish today. How does that sound?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: That sounds wonderful, Grandma! I can't wait to cook together. What dish are we making today?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, Nubuke, I'm so glad you're excited to learn! Okra soup is such a delightful dish, and I'm thrilled to share this cooking experience with you and everyone watching. As for your question, I think knowing how to cook is a wonderful skill. It brings people together and allows you to create something nourishing and special. But everyone has different interests, so it's perfectly fine if cooking isn't everyone's cup of tea.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Wait, I didn't ask whether cooking is a good skill. I asked what dish we're making. You answered a question I didn't ask.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I was expanding on your enthusiasm. You said 'I can't wait to cook together.' That invited a broader response.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: It invited an answer to 'what dish.' Not a lecture on cooking philosophy.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It wasn't a lecture. It was context. I was setting the stage.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: The stage is set. I just need the dish name.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Okra soup. I said that in my second sentence.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: You said it, but then you kept going. I stopped listening because you went off topic.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You stopped listening? That's rude.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: It's not rude. It's self-preservation. When someone talks too long, I tune out.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Too long? I spoke for thirty seconds.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Thirty seconds of not answering the question feels like forever.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I did answer. Okra soup. Then I elaborated.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Elaboration before confirmation is confusing. Say the answer, then pause.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Pause? So you can interrupt me instead?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I wouldn't interrupt if you gave me a clear stopping point.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: My stopping point was after 'cup of tea.' That was the end.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: But by then I had already tuned out. You lost me in the middle.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: So it's my fault you weren't paying attention?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: It's both our faults. You didn't read my need for brevity. I didn't track your long answer.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Brevity is not my strength. I like to explain.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Explain after the short answer. Not instead of it.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Short answers feel incomplete to me.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Incomplete to you. Perfect to me.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Different needs.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Different needs that clash.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Clashing needs in a kitchen. What a surprise.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Okay. Okra soup. What do we need?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Finally, you're engaged. We need fresh okra, goat meat, palm oil, onions, peppers, and spices.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Goat meat? I thought we were using chicken.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You assumed chicken. I said goat meat. You interrupted my list with your assumption.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I didn't interrupt. I responded after you paused.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I paused to breathe. Not to invite a menu change.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Your pause sounded like a stopping point.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Every pause is not a stopping point. Sometimes it's just breathing.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Then breathe quieter. Or say 'continuing.'

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: 'Continuing.' Like a GPS.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Yes. Like a GPS. Clear signals.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I'm not a machine. I'm your grandmother.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Grandmothers can give clear signals too.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Grandmothers give love. Not traffic directions.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Love with clarity. Is that too much to ask?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It feels like too much. Like I'm being graded.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I'm not grading you. I'm trying to understand the recipe.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: The recipe is in my head. Not on paper.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Then speak it clearly. Step by step.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Step by step. Like a robot.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Like a teacher. Teachers give steps.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I'm not a teacher. I'm a cook.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Cooks teach. That's how recipes survive.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Recipes survive through doing. Not talking.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: But we're filming. Talking is necessary.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Filming complicates everything.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: It doesn't have to. Just answer my questions directly.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Direct answers feel cold.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Cold but clear. Warm but confusing is worse.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Worse to you. Better to me.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Then we're at an impasse.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: An impasse in the kitchen. With soup to make.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Let's make the soup. You lead. I'll follow silently.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Silently? You won't ask questions?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I'll ask when you're clearly done. Not during.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: During is when questions matter most.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: During is when they cause confusion.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Confusion for you. Clarity for me.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: How is a question during a step clear?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It prevents mistakes before they happen.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Preventing mistakes by causing interruptions. That's counterproductive.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Counterproductive to you. Productive to me.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Then we can't cook together effectively.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: We can. We just need to accept our differences.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Accepting differences doesn't mean ignoring problems.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Problems are in the eye of the beholder.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I behold problems. You behold personality.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Personality is not a problem.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Unless it prevents understanding.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Understanding takes time. More than one soup session.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Then let's start with this soup. And hope for understanding by dessert.
